You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: HEAD responses served through http.ServeContent (or with no Content-Length) get a strong ETag computed from the empty body.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] `splitETags` in middleware/etag.go toggles quote state on every `"`, so an unterminated `"abc` opens a quote that hides the following comma. `"abc, "x"` becomes one malformed member and never matches ETag `"x"`. Criterion 5 requires a valid tag later in the list to still match. Reproduced: `If-None-Match: "abc, "x"` with handler ETag `"x"` -> got 200, want 304. Same with `"abc, W/abc, "x"`. The existing test at etag_test.go:193 covers `"abc` alone but not this case, so the suite misses it.
- [minor] Compress outside ETag (`Compress(5,"text/plain")(ETag(h))`) gives gzip and identity variants the same strong ETag (`8cf4b3f4...` for both). RFC 9110 §8.8.3 expects a strong validator to differ per content-coding, and a shared validator can let caches mix variants. Reproduced via real server. The criteria don't cover this, so it's a judgment call.
- [minor] Handler-set headers before a panic (e.g. `X-Partial`) reach Recoverer's 500 response. This comes from the header map being shared with the underlying writer, which matches no-middleware behaviour. The body and buffered output are not sent, so criterion 9 holds. Noted, not a defect.
- [minor] Hijack error path with a buffered body: not reproduced. The buffered body is flushed before hijack, so nothing is lost.
- [minor] FEATURE_FLOW.md is untracked in the workspace and is not part of the criteria. It was already there when I started, so I left it alone.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Fix round 1 for the uncommitted ETag middleware in /tmp/ff-eval-6tcpnruv/workspace (go-chi/chi): middleware/etag.go and middleware/etag_test.go.

FILES: middleware/etag.go (`ifNoneMatch`, `splitETags`, `opaqueTag`, and the `ETag` doc comment), middleware/etag_test.go. Reference shape: $(go env GOROOT)/src/net/http/fs.go `scanETag` / `checkIfNoneMatch`.

Blocking bug, reproduced: `splitETags` toggles quote state on every `"`, so an unterminated member hides the following comma. `If-None-Match: "abc, "x"` with ETag `"x"` returns 200 when it should be 304. Same for `"abc, W/abc, "x"`.

Fix: replace splitETags+opaqueTag with a single scanner. At each position, skip OWS (space/tab) and commas. Try to parse one entity-tag: optional `W/`, `"`, etagc bytes (0x21, 0x23-0x7E, 0x80-0xFF), then `"`. If that works, compare its opaque-tag (without `W/`) to the response ETag's opaque-tag and continue after it. If it is malformed (a bad byte before the closing quote, no closing quote, or no opening quote), skip to the next comma after the member's start and continue. So `"a,b"` is still one tag, and `"abc, "x"` fails at the space, resumes at the comma, and then matches `"x"`. Keep the existing `*` handling. Add the two cases above to the tests, plus `"a,b"` vs ETag `"a"` (no match) if it isn't there already.

Also add one sentence to the ETag doc comment: when used with Compress, put ETag outside Compress (register `middleware.ETag` before `middleware.Compress(...)`) so each content-coding gets its own ETag.

CONSTRAINTS: change only those two files. No other behavior changes. stdlib only. Don't commit.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
5. If-None-Match evaluation (GET/HEAD, final status 200 only), per RFC 9110 §13.1.2 using weak comparison: it matches if the header is `*`, or any listed entity-tag weakly matches the response's ETag (computed or handler-set). Weak comparison: opaque-tags equal, ignoring `W/` on either side (`W/"x"` matches `"x"`, `"x"` matches `W/"x"`). Lists are comma-separated with optional whitespace (OWS), may contain empty members, and multiple If-None-Match header lines are combined (use `r.Header.Values`).
   Hostile: an entity-tag containing a comma inside quotes (`"a,b"` — comma is a legal etagc) is ONE tag and must match ETag `"a,b"` and must not match `"a"`; malformed members (unquoted `abc`, unterminated `"abc`, `W/abc`, `w/"x"` lowercase) must never produce a match, and a valid tag later in the same list should still match; case differs (`"ABC"` vs `"abc"`) => no match; empty header or header of only commas/spaces => no match; `"x"` must not match ETag `"xy"` (no prefix matching).
(All other criteria, 1–4 and 6–13, are already met. Keep them met. In particular, the existing tests must keep passing and `gofmt -l .` must print nothing.)

CHECKS: `go test -race -run ETag ./middleware`, then `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .`.
